LogEx query bitmap allocation seam (Roaring 0.10.12)

source, tests, manifests, upstream lockfile and original README. No upgrade.

New API (std feature only)
- RoaringBitmap::prepare_deserialize(&[u8]) -> io::Result<bitmap::PreparedBitmap>
- PreparedBitmap::allocation_bytes() -> usize
- PreparedBitmap::deserialize(self) -> io::Result<RoaringBitmap>
- RoaringBitmap::heap_size_bytes() -> io::Result<usize>

Preparation validates cookie/count, keys, exact offsets/extents, sparse ordering,
dense popcount, and ordered/disjoint/nonoverflowing runs with exact cardinality.
It borrows immutable bytes and allocates no heap storage on success. The checked
preflight size counts requested container Vec slots plus normalized array Vecs
or 8192-byte dense boxes. Decoding has no heap scratch allocations. Sparse runs
fill exact-cardinality arrays directly; dense runs fill one zeroed bitmap box,
preventing the ordinary generic run route's oversized array representation.
Serialized dense data uses the existing full-buffer direct constructor: no new
zero-fill/intermediate copy and no new unsafe code. Release builds reuse the
validated cardinality; upstream debug assertions revalidate constructor content.

Heap measurement includes actual container Vec and u16 array Vec capacities plus
8192 per dense box; it excludes allocator headers/stack/struct size. It does not
use statistics() (whose historical byte fields have different units). Callers
reserve preflight bytes before decoding, then reconcile allocator-returned Vec
capacities while owning both bitmap and reservation. This seam is dependency-
independent and does not itself impose a budget or process-RSS bound. Controlled clone, union/intersection and narrow reference MultiOps are described
below. Range construction, filtering, difference and XOR are outside this patch.

Five new lib tests exercise empty/sparse/dense boundaries, key65535, normalized
singleton/full runs, mixed and unaligned payloads, malformed/truncated geometry,
array/run/dense content validation, checked arithmetic, and spare heap capacity.
Run parity checks compare rows and cardinality, not structural Store equality:
the generic decoder may retain an oversized array whereas the query decoder
normalizes the same set into a bitmap. Explicit Store shape and independently
generated expected rows are tested separately.
Existing upstream tests remain present. Standard validation command:
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/roaring-regressions cargo test --manifest-path vendor/roaring/Cargo.toml --lib --locked

The unmodified published vendor lock requires upstream dev-dependencies, including
postcard even without enabling serde. An offline run requires those exact locked
packages cached. Root workspace uses its existing versions via the path override;
its lock change only removes roaring's registry source/checksum.

Verify inventory against the archive hash above, verify unchanged files against
LOGEX-UPSTREAM-SHA256, review LOGEX-PATCH.diff and the added source/license
file hashes in the repository vendor verifier. Re-audit the private representation
and constructors before replacing/upgrading the pinned crate or enabling SIMD.

B3b controlled operations (query_ops.rs, std only)
- QuerySetOp::{Union,Intersection}
- prepare_clone() -> PreparedClone; allocation_bytes(), materialize(observer)
- prepare_assign(&mut self, &rhs, op) -> PreparedAssign;
  additional_allocation_bytes(), apply(observer)
- prepare_owned_assign(&mut self, &mut rhs, op) -> PreparedOwnedAssign;
  additional_allocation_bytes(), apply(observer); empties RHS on success
- RoaringBitmap::prepare_union_refs(&[&RoaringBitmap]) -> PreparedUnionRefs;
  allocation_bytes(), materialize(observer); rejects key spans >=8
All preparation/application methods are fallible. The observer receives requested
and actual capacity bytes once for each newly created Vec before filling or
installation. An observer failure drops that locally owned allocation before
returning. Keep input allocations and their charges alive through mutation;
owned operations require both input charges to remain held, even after a store
moves. On error or unwind, an apply-only drop guard resets mutable operands to empty
after local temporary values unwind, preserving public bitmap invariants. Dropping
a preparation without applying leaves operands unchanged. Borrowed RHS never
changes. No catch-unwind is used in production.
On success dispose RHS backing and reconcile the combined charge to actual heap.

Allowances are checked requested-capacity envelopes: explicit destination-vector
replacement plus concrete per-container union allocations; intersection's largest
single-container scratch overlap (with cumulative SIMD retained tail allowance).
No blanket dense-per-key allowance applies to pairwise sparse union. Allocator
excess is observed after allocation; callers must account it immediately and
retain that excess until final heap reconciliation. This deliberately matches
cooperative allocation accounting, not a hard RSS cap. Fixed dense boxes require
8192 bytes; allocator headers, stack and control structs are excluded.

Owned union preserves the row-cardinality swap, disjoint container moves and
mixed-store dense reuse. Owned intersection preserves the container-count swap,
smaller-array reuse, and inplace scalar retention. Borrowed operations preserve
borrowed payload cloning. The existing scalar/SIMD kernels are reused through
preallocated VecWriter storage; SIMD receives seven u16 spare tail slots because
its vector visitor writes eight lanes before truncation. Ordinary methods and
operator implementations are unchanged.

Reference union keeps upstream prefix sorting (all inputs up to50; first10 when
larger) and Cow lazy dense promotion. Explicit reference/Cow/output vector
capacities and dense-to-array overlap are included. Inputs are borrowed from a
stable reference slice, whose caller-owned allocation is separately charged.
The key-span restriction is validated before materialization.

Six focused logex_query_ops tests cover owned/borrowed set semantics, sparse
allowances, moved allocation identities, threshold normalization/spare capacity,
reference prefix boundaries and lazy promotions, and observer rejection/unwind points, including valid-empty reset semantics.
These are additive; upstream tests remain unchanged. SIMD retains its existing
nightly-only feature requirement and needs a compatible toolchain for execution.

SIMD validation limitation (explicit, unchanged upstream code): enabling --features
simd on repository-pinned nightly-2026-08-24 fails before tests at original
store/array_store/vector.rs:16: core::simd::LaneCount and SupportedLaneCount are
no longer exported (E0432). The default non-SIMD feature path is tested. SIMD is
not enabled by LogEx; no toolchain change, runtime feature change or upstream SIMD
compatibility rewrite is included. The controlled cfg path retains dispatch and
its audited seven-element temporary vector-store allowance, but is not claimed
runtime-validated on this compiler.
